CLASS 30 · PRESCHOOL AGES 4–5

Logic, Thinking & Problem-Solving

Age 4–5 YearsClass 30 of 30Adventures 30 logic gamesSubjects Patterns · clues · sorting

Build early reasoning, observation, memory, matching, sequencing, sorting, and problem-solving skills through playful picture puzzles. Thirty real games — every one played on its own puzzle illustration, with spoken instructions and a printable worksheet twin in the Logic worksheet library.

Patterns to finish, odd ones to catch, shadows to match, mazes to trace and codes to crack — every puzzle spoken aloud, every answer a picture.

Meet the adventures ↓Puzzles are best in short, happy sittings.

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

Little puzzles in big kitchens.

Sock-drawer sorting

  • Sort socks by size or pattern — real objects, real sorting, real pride.
  • Ask “how did you decide?” and let the rule be theirs.

What comes next, snack edition

  • Line up apple, grape, apple, grape… and let your child place the next one.
  • Swap in crackers, berries or cheese cubes once the pattern clicks.

Logic at four is playful rules: same and different, first and last, big and small. The kitchen is full of all three.

A NOTE FROM THE PRINCIPAL

For the grown-ups.

Logic games teach children that rules are things you can spot, name and use. Every puzzle here shows its rule in pictures, speaks its question aloud, and answers a wrong tap with a hint instead of a buzzer — the habit being built is trying a rule again, not fear of getting it wrong.

The printable worksheets twin every game with room to draw, sort and circle. Browse the logic worksheets — and remember, downloading never marks a class complete; only finished games do, and only for the child chosen in My Classroom.
